original_metadata.title: Over the formal field Q(alpha), the infinite quantum Benjamin-Ono Lax resolvent on symmetric functions equals the ratio-defined Jack-diagonal Hamiltonian generating series coefficientwise on every fixed degree
original_metadata.author: Maxim Nazarov; Evgeny Sklyanin
original_metadata.source_title: Integrable Hierarchy of the Quantum Benjamin-Ono Equation
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The main proof constructs a Baker-Akhiezer operator vector and proves its full monomial-symmetric-function formula through a tensor-symbol identity, split by partition length and the formal parameter alpha. It then establishes the Lax resolvent identity by adjoint symmetric-function calculations and multiplicity cancellations, connecting an explicit infinite differential-operator hierarchy with the Jack spectral family beyond ordinary qualification techniques.

proof_review.note: Full Theorem2 I(u)=p(u-L)^(-1)p* is selected with alpha an indeterminate and the symmetric-function algebra over Q(alpha), as in Section5. The inverse is the formal u^(-1) expansion and every coefficient is locally finite on fixed homogeneous degree, explicitly checked immediately after (6.3)/(6.4); no analytic infinite-matrix inverse or all singular complex alpha values is claimed. Read Section3-6 definitions/adjoints and prior A(u) eigenvalues, the full new Theorem3 Baker-Akhiezer support and Proposition1 on pages8-9, and every Section8 tensor-symbol/partition-length/alpha-coefficient/cancellation step and Propositions2-3 on pages9-13. Prior published [9] Theorem1 formula for A^(k) and standard Macdonald symmetric-function identities are cited background, rather than unexpanded new local core. Theorem3 is bundled only as support; individual commuting Hamiltonians, the classical limit, and low-order instances are not counted separately.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full formal Theorem2 on Lambda over Q(alpha), alpha indeterminate. A(u) is the Jack-diagonal series (5.4)-(5.5), I(u) is defined by 1-u^(-1)I(u)=A(u)/A(u+1), p_n*=alpha n partial/partial p_n, p_0=0 and p_-n=p_n*. The infinite Lax matrix is L_ij=j(alpha-1)delta_ij+p_(j-i). Then I(u)=p(u-L)^(-1)p*, with formal u^(-1) inverse; the locally finite coefficient expression (6.4) acts on each fixed degree. No Hilbert-space analytic self-adjointness, convergence of a numerical resolvent, or arbitrary specialized alpha is selected.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: Editorial note only: (8.3) writes Phi_n^(k) within its sum where the immediately preceding (8.2) and following explicitly rewritten sums use the indexed Phi_i and Phi_(n+i), Phi_(n-i). The fully displayed symbol identity (8.5) and subsequent cancellation proof retain those indices, so the selected formal operator identity is unambiguously scoped. Equation(3.6) also repeats mu as a summation index while its preceding refinement definition and cited identity fix the intended monomial expansion. Source bytes and formulas remain unchanged.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: Full original Theorem 2 formal Lax-resolvent identity is retained with all symmetric-function/adjoint/Jack Hamiltonian conventions, the new Baker-Akhiezer Theorem 3 and Proposition 1 support and the complete tensor-symbol, partition-length, alpha-coefficient and cancellation proof. Alpha is an indeterminate over Q(alpha); the matrix inverse is the formal u-inverse series and each coefficient acts locally finitely on fixed degree. The original ratio definition of I(u) is supplied. Prior published A(u) formula and standard Macdonald identities remain cited background. Original indexed-symbol and repeated-index slips remain unchanged with their notices. No analytic infinite-matrix inverse, singular complex-alpha specialization, classical limit or individual Hamiltonian count is selected.
